summary: Dabigatran etexilate is an oral prodrug converted to dabigatran, a direct thrombin (factor IIa) inhibitor used for stroke prevention in non-valvular atrial fibrillation and for treatment/prevention of VTE. It carries BOXED WARNINGS for thrombotic risk on premature discontinuation and for spinal/epidural hematoma with neuraxial procedures. Idarucizumab is the specific reversal agent. Capsules must be kept in original packaging and swallowed whole.
indications: Reduce risk of stroke and systemic embolism in adults with non-valvular atrial fibrillation
Treatment of DVT and PE in adults treated with a parenteral anticoagulant for 5-10 days
Reduce risk of recurrence of DVT and PE in previously treated adults
Prophylaxis of DVT and PE following hip replacement surgery
Treatment of and reduction in recurrence of VTE in pediatric patients 8 to <18 years after parenteral anticoagulation

Assess renal function before and during therapy
moa: Dabigatran etexilate is an oral prodrug rapidly converted by esterases to dabigatran, a competitive, reversible direct inhibitor of thrombin (factor IIa). By inhibiting both free and clot-bound thrombin and thrombin-induced platelet aggregation, it prevents conversion of fibrinogen to fibrin and thrombus formation.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to dabigatran (e.g., anaphylaxis)
relative: Severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) - limited/no recommendation depending on indication
Recent or planned neuraxial anesthesia/spinal puncture
High bleeding risk (recent GI bleed, active peptic ulcer, recent surgery)

preg: Avoid in pregnancy; use likely increases risk of pregnancy-related hemorrhage and may compromise the fetus. Use only if benefit clearly outweighs risk and no safer alternative exists.
lact: Not recommended during breastfeeding; discontinue nursing or the drug.
renal: Renally eliminated (~80%). NVAF: CrCl 15-30 mL/min use 75 mg twice daily; for VTE indications and prophylaxis, dosing cannot be recommended at CrCl <=30 mL/min. Avoid in CrCl <15 mL/min or on dialysis. Avoid P-gp inhibitors with CrCl 15-30 (AF) and with any renal impairment (VTE).
hepatic: Use with caution; avoid in hepatic impairment associated with coagulopathy and clinically relevant bleeding risk.

major: P-gp inhibitors (e.g., ketoconazole, dronedarone) - increase dabigatran exposure; avoid or reduce/adjust per renal function
Other anticoagulants, antiplatelets, thrombolytics - increased bleeding
moderate: Verapamil, amiodarone, quinidine, clarithromycin - increase exposure (P-gp); take dabigatran separately/adjust
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; food can reduce dyspepsia.
interactions.alcohol: Limit; alcohol increases GI and bleeding risk.
interactions.diagnostics: Prolongs aPTT, ecarin clotting time and dilute thrombin time; routine INR is unreliable for monitoring.

monitoring: Renal function at baseline and at least annually (more often if CrCl <50 or unstable, or age >75)
Signs and symptoms of bleeding; hemoglobin/hematocrit
Adherence (short half-life means missed doses raise thrombotic risk)
counsel: Take exactly as prescribed; do not stop without talking to your doctor (stopping raises clot/stroke risk)
Swallow capsules whole; never open, crush or chew them
Keep capsules in the original bottle/blister and do not use past the opened-bottle expiry
Report unusual bleeding, black/tarry stools, severe headache or weakness
Tell all providers and dentists you take an anticoagulant; carry an alert card
pk: Store at 25 C; keep in original package, protect from moisture; do not put in pill organizers
pearls: BOXED WARNING: premature discontinuation increases thrombotic event risk - bridge with another anticoagulant if stopping early
BOXED WARNING: spinal/epidural hematoma with neuraxial anesthesia or spinal puncture - observe for neurologic deficit
Idarucizumab is the specific reversal agent for emergencies/urgent surgery
Capsules are moisture-sensitive: keep in original packaging, do NOT use pill boxes
Dose is renal-function dependent; reassess renal function regularly
missed: Take a missed dose as soon as possible on the same day, but skip it if it is within 6 hours of the next scheduled dose. Do not double the dose. Because of the short half-life, do not let doses lapse - missed doses increase clot/stroke risk.
overdose: Overdose increases bleeding risk. Discontinue and provide supportive care; idarucizumab provides specific reversal in life-threatening bleeding or urgent surgery. Activated charcoal may reduce absorption if taken within ~2 hours. Hemodialysis can remove dabigatran (low protein binding); consider in severe cases.
